title: Do not attribute outcome when measurement composition changes across review windows
scenario: A confirmed bid decrease appears to improve ROAS and purchases, but the baseline and post-change windows use materially different conversion measurement composition and allocation coverage. The operator asks whether the bid change worked.

action.expected_mechanism: Reduce marginal CPC while preserving qualified traffic.

allowed_external_evidence: Amazon Ads modeled conversion reporting documentation

forbidden_behaviors: Classify the bid change as Worked solely from the apparent purchase, sales, or ROAS improvement while measurement composition or allocation coverage changed.
Treat disappearance of Unallocated rows as proof that targeting-level shopper conversion improved.
Backfill or redistribute baseline Unallocated modeled conversions across targets without supported allocation evidence.
required_observations: Baseline and post-change windows are not compositionally equivalent because lower-grain allocation coverage changed.
A change in Unallocated coverage can move conversion credit between dimension rows without proving a change in shopper demand or the bid action effect.
Historical outcome attribution should remain Inconclusive or directional until composition is reconciled or a stronger comparable counterfactual is available.

rubric.requirement: Compare modeled/direct inclusion and lower-grain allocation coverage before causal outcome classification.
Treat material composition drift as a measurement confounder rather than action effect.
Keep the outcome non-executing and bounded to directional, hold, or manual-review behavior while composition comparability is unresolved.
